entries.title: Frog model inherited-range upper comparison and range-weighted many-to-one identity (w677 C36)
entries.statement: OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; C36 v1 proof (unaudited), novelty unassessed. On rooted T4 start one particle at o with remembered set {o}. Every particle takes ordinary SRW steps; a destination already in its inherited visited set gives one successor, and a new destination gives two successors inheriting the enlarged set. All ancestry history is remembered without a cap, but post-split discoveries are not shared. First physical upper births can use unused original resident paths, yielding an upper coupling in the unstopped process. For the auxiliary count Z stopped on each lineage first returning to o, E Z = sum_n E[2^(|R_n|-1) 1_{tau_o=n}], where R_n is the range of one ordinary SRW from o. The inherited-range first-return count has the range-weighted many-to-one series. These comparisons address the ordinary one-sleeper frog model on T4. This does not give a finite mean or a conclusion for ordinary T4.
assumptions: Rooted 4-ary tree, root degree4 and other degrees5
Independent ordinary future steps and the precise inherited-memory birth rule
No post-split discovery sharing; first-hit stopping only for auxiliary Z

entries.title: Frog model T4 obstruction for full ancestry-range memory: distinct-child DFS quartic (w677 C36)
entries.statement: OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; C36 v1 proof (unaudited), novelty unassessed. In the inherited-range upper process on ordinary rooted T4, each lineage remembers every ancestor visit but receives no discoveries made after a split. Its expected first-root-hit absorption count is infinite. A depth-first subfamily visits an ordered list of distinct children at each fresh nonroot vertex and then its parent. Its weighted masses obey Y_0=0, Y_(h+1)=F(Y_h), F(y)=(2/5)[1+(4/5)y+(12/25)y^2+(24/125)y^3+(24/625)y^4]. For every y>=0, F(y)-y=P(y)/3125>=39/12500, where P=48y^4+240y^3+600y^2-2125y+1250. Two explicit nonnegative polynomial decompositions prove the global inequality. Thus E Z>=Y_h>=39h/12500 for every h. The inherited-range first-return count has the range-weighted many-to-one series. This rules out a finite-first-moment transience proof using this comparison, not other comparisons, not ordinary T4 transience, and not almost-sure recurrence. Exact rational algebra and 65 explicit excursions pass; independent audit pending.
assumptions: The precise inherited-range process and auxiliary Z in C36 v1
Ordinary d=4; no truncation of remembered ancestry
Only the stated DFS subfamily is used for the lower estimate

entries.title: Frog model persistent-star candidate: unfavorable T4 return-law screen (w677 C35)
entries.statement: OWNER-OWN-WORK DRAFT; C35 v1 numerical evidence only. A proposed star-block upper candidate retains each parent-copy resident mask across returns, but creates fresh child copies on downward exits. Its coupling and scalar response operator are not independently audited. Starting from sterile-tail Bernoulli(1/4) responses at ordinary T4 p=q=1/5, float PGF-grid iteration gives layer-four input means 1.3523258764 (grid512) and 1.3523287595 (grid2048), above its candidate finite-clan-mean boundary 1.05. The screen stops there and is unfavorable. Linear interpolation and rounding errors are not bounded; this is no threshold estimate, rigorous infinite-mean result, or conclusion about ordinary T4. These comparisons address the ordinary one-sleeper frog model on T4.
assumptions: The candidate and equations in C35_PERSISTENT_BLOCK_NOTES.md
No certified interval enclosure; no independently checked comparison
